U: › [ U ] an amount of money that a person who has been accused of a crime pays to a law court so that they can be released until their trial. The payment is a way of making certain that the person will return to court for trial

T: › [ T ] If someone accused of a crime is bailed, they are released until their trial after paying bail to the court.

NONE: › the two small pieces of wood on top of the stumps in a game of cricket, that can be knocked off with the ball to make the player who is batting (= hitting the ball) out
（板球）三柱門上的橫木

I: › [ I ] UK also bale to remove water from a boat using a container

example: Because of a previous conviction, the judge refused to grant bail (= allow the accused person to be released).
由於嫌犯有前科，法官不准將他保釋。
The boat's sinking! Start bailing quickly!
船在下沉！快往外舀水！
She was yesterday bailed for three weeks on drink-driving offences.
酒後駕駛被捕之後，她昨天獲准保釋三個星期。
[ + to infinitive ] He was bailed to appear at the Magistrates' Court next month.
他獲准保釋，定於下個月在地方法院出庭。

NONE: › to jump out of an aircraft with a parachute because the aircraft is going to have an accident
（因飛機失事）跳傘
› mainly US to stop doing or being involved with something
放棄，退出

example: The plane's engine failed and the pilot was forced to bail out.
飛機引擎發生故障，機師被迫跳傘。
The actor has bailed out of the film after only three weeks' shooting.
該演員只拍攝了三個星期就退演了。

NONE: › to pay money to a court so that someone can be released from prison until their trial
把（某人）保釋出來
› to help a person or organization that is in difficulty, usually by giving or lending them money
（通常指在經濟上）幫助（某人或機構）脫離困境；金援

example: She keeps running up huge debts and asking friends to bail her out.
她不斷欠下巨額的債務，最後總是要請朋友們幫忙。

NONE: › to remove water from the bottom of a boat
（從船中）往外舀水
› the open area inside the outer wall of a castle
（中世紀城堡的）郭；（城堡與外郭之間的）堡場
› (in the UK ) an official who takes away someone's possessions when they owe money
（英國查封財產的）查封官，執行官
› (in the UK ) a person whose job is to take care of someone else's land or property
（英國）莊園管家
› (in the US) an official who is responsible for prisoners who are appearing in court
（美國）法警，庭吏

example: They didn't pay their rent, so the landlord called/sent in the bailiffs.
他們欠著房租沒付，所以房東叫來了執行官。

NONE: › the area that a person or an organization is interested in, is responsible for, or controls
活動（或興趣、知識、權利）範圍
› the act of helping a person or organization that is in difficulty, usually by giving or giving or lending money
（通常指從經濟上）幫助（某人或機構）脫離困境

example: Three years of huge losses forced the bank to seek a government bailout.
長達三年的巨額虧損迫使銀行向政府尋求援助。
The administration assembled the $50 billion emergency bailout package to ease a financial crisis in Mexico.
管理部門籌劃了一連串總值達500億美元的緊急經濟緩助計劃，以舒緩墨西哥的金融危機。

NONE: bail noun(CRICKET)
› a child
兒童，小孩

U: › [ U ] a small amount of food on a hook (= curved piece of wire) or in a special device used to attract and catch a fish or animal

T: › to put food on a hook (= curved piece of wire) or in a special device to attract and catch a fish or animal

C or U: › [ C or U ] something that is said or offered to people in order to make them react in a particular way

T: › to intentionally make a person angry by saying or doing things to annoy them
› to make dogs attack an animal for cruel entertainment

example: They were digging up worms to use for bait.
他們在挖蟲子製餌。
We put down some poisoned bait to kill the rats.
我們放了一些毒餌滅鼠。
Free holidays were offered as (a) bait to customers.
以免費度假來吸引顧客。
I told my sister I'd lend her my new shirt if she let me borrow her jacket, but she didn't take the bait.
我跟姐姐說，如果她能把夾克借給我，我就把新襯衫借給她，可是她不為所動。
Ignore him - he's just baiting you.
別理他——他存心惹你生氣呢。
I suspect he was just baiting me.
我懷疑他只是在故意激我。
Do you have any stale cheese that I can bait the mousetrap with?
你有沒有已經變味的起司？我想放在捕鼠器上作餌。

NONE: › thick, usually green material made from wool and used to cover the special tables on which snooker, billiards, and card games are played
（通常是綠色的）枱面呢
